summary: Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). The cost in the finding is gone. There was one Node child per lookup with no cache, and each icon was resolved twice (HTTP before config, then RPC). Now every server path, HTTP /api/project-favicon and RPC projects.readIcon (web and mobile), goes through one ProjectFaviconResolver. It has a 10-min TTL cache, per-root single-flight, and 2 reader fibers that batch up to 16 roots per killable child. The web client shows a placeholder until the server config is known and only uses HTTP for servers without the projectIcons capability. The client cache is now keyed by environment+project+revision, so it survives reconnects. Server-side caching also removes the warm-reload RPC spawns the original verifier flagged. No other caller spawns per lookup, and the Hub only relays projects.readIcon. A critical read found only minor fix defects (below), none of which restore the per-project spawn cost.

evidence.note: 10-min TTL, 60 s stalled-root backoff, 1024-entry cap, 2 reader children, 16 roots per child, 30 s caller deadline. This replaces the old Semaphore(2) with no cache (git show f1be4abc7).
Readers use Queue.takeBetween(queue, 1, 16): one child per batch, not per project.
readIcon returns a cache hit, or joins or registers a pending Deferred and enqueues the root once (single-flight shared by HTTP and RPC).
Per-root results. The first unfinished root gets a 60 s null backoff, and the roots after it get one retry child.

readProjectFavicons(roots) uses one execFile child per batch: deadline 1.5 s + 250 ms per extra root, SIGKILL, partial stdout parsed per line. The isolation the verifier required is kept. argv.slice(1) layout checked under both node and bun --eval.
The worker resolves every root in order and writes one JSON line per root as it goes.
The HTTP favicon route uses the same resolver.readIcon.
The RPC path uses the same resolver.readIcon(project.workspaceRoot). It is wired from apps/server/src/ws/projectRpc.ts:43-46.
config == null or deferred gives src null (placeholder). HTTP is used only when the RPC capability is absent and the row is visible. This removes the HTTP-then-RPC double resolve.
The read is gated on viewport intersection and checks peekProjectIconSource first.

Per-environment LRU keyed by project+revision (no longer by connection generation), 5-min TTL, pending single-flight. Mobile uses the same module (apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:43-59).
Defect: Effect.tryPromise(() => options.readFavicons(roots)) drops the AbortSignal. The old code passed { signal } (f1be4abc7 resolver line 14), so interrupting a reader no longer SIGKILLs its child.
Defect: the cache has an entry cap but no byte cap, and is keyed on the raw cwd string. Expired entries are never pruned until capacity eviction.

fixDefects: All minor, none restores the per-project spawn cost. (1) The resolver no longer propagates interruption to the child. ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:69 calls Effect.tryPromise(() => options.readFavicons(roots)) and ReadProjectFavicons (lines 22-24) has no signal parameter. The old resolver passed { signal } to readProjectFavicon. When the resolver scope closes (server shutdown), an in-flight child is not SIGKILLed at once. It is bounded only by execFile's own timeout while the parent lives, and is orphaned if the parent exits first. readProjectFavicons still supports signal and the abort tests still pass, but production never uses it. (2) The server cache (lines 37-48) caps entries at 1024 but has no byte budget. Found icons keep up to 512 KB each (readProjectFavicon.ts:15), so the worst case is about 512 MB. The key is the raw cwd string, and the authenticated HTTP route accepts any cwd (http.ts:744-750), so aliases such as '/p', '/p/', '/p/.' each miss and each take an entry. Expired entries stay until capacity eviction. Realistic single-user memory is small. (3) The stalled-root heuristic (lines 84-93) blames the first root of a batch even when the whole child failed: spawn error, or Node/Electron startup slower than the 1.5 s deadline under boot load. That root gets a 60 s null. The RPC result cannot express 'unavailable', so the client caches that null as a known absence for 5 min (projectIconSource.ts:96-104), and that now survives reconnects because the cache is no longer per connection generation. (4) As the auditor noted, there is no mtime/realpath invalidation: a newly added favicon appears after up to 10 min server-side plus 5 min client-side. Each cold miss still pays one Node startup per batch rather than using a long-lived worker. That is acceptable given the kill-ability requirement.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening, all in apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts (plus a small readProjectFavicon.ts change). (a) Change ReadProjectFavicons to (roots, signal?: AbortSignal). Use Effect.tryPromise((signal) => options.readFavicons(roots, signal)), and pass { signal } in makeProjectFaviconResolver to readProjectFavicons. Test: an injected reader records the signal; close the scope mid-read and assert signal.aborted. (b) Normalize the cache/pending key with path.resolve(cwd), a pure string operation with no FS I/O, so the isolation stays intact. Track retained bytes in remember() and evict oldest entries until under a budget (for example 32 MB) as well as the 1024-entry cap. Optionally sweep expired entries in remember(). Tests: '/p', '/p/' and '/p/.' share one batch entry; a byte budget smaller than 3 icons evicts the oldest. (c) Make readProjectFavicons report whether the child wrote any line or hit its deadline (for example, return { results, childRan: boolean }). In readBatch, apply STALLED_ROOT_BACKOFF_MS only when the child produced output or timed out, not when the spawn itself failed. Optionally, in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts, cache null results with a shorter TTL (for example 60 s) than found artwork, so a transient server-side null does not hide an icon for 5 min. Run the focused vitest files apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.test.ts and apps/server/src/project/readProjectFavicon.test.ts, plus the client-runtime projectIconSource tests if (c) touches them.
decisionReason: Server-internal cache and child-lifecycle hardening. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle, or Hub protocol impact, and the RPC contract is unchanged.
correction: The auditor's DONE is correct. Corrections: (1) Several cited line ranges have drifted: resolver readIcon is at 113-129 (not 123-137), readers at 96-111, the worker loop at projectFaviconWorker.ts:98-112, ProjectFavicon src logic at 108-128, readProjectIcon resolver call at line 32. (2) The auditor missed that the fix dropped AbortSignal propagation to the child (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:69). (3) The auditor missed that the server cache has no byte budget and uses the raw-cwd key. (4) The auditor missed that a whole-child failure blames the first root, and that this null is then pinned by the client for 5 min across reconnects.
